# Task plans — `<repo>/Resource/plans/`, the one home

Executed motion for a task: joint trajectories, sub-trajectory boundaries and
final actions. One JSON per `<task>_<arm>_<mode>`, e.g.
`bottomlid_left_ruckig_pro_only.json`.

These are **artifacts, not source**. A plan is the output of running a task
config through a planner; the config is what gets authored and reviewed. They
are committed because the Studio's Schedule & Run tab resolves a step to its
plan, and `segment_verifier` treats four of them as the contract.

**Who writes here.** The `alix_tasks` task node
(`src/common/task_base.cpp`, `savePlannedTrajectory`) saves every plan it
records into `Resource/plans/<fixture>/<source>/`, locating the repo root by
marker (`ARCHITECTURE.md` + `ros/`, D8) or `ALIX_REPO_ROOT`. Readers go
through `alix_taskgen.paths.plan_roots()`, which lists this directory first.
Nothing reads plans from the package share, and `plans` is not in the
package's `install(DIRECTORY …)`.

**ALIX Studio Lite runs commode C's lid and seat plans** (`commode_c/hardware/`
`lid_open`, `seat_open`, `seat_close`, `lid_close`, their `_seq` sequence plans,
`rungs/lid_open_*`) and their configs (`mechanism_tasks/commode_c/<task>.yaml`)
from its own copies. After changing any of them, on either side, run Lite's
`python3 tools/mechanism_sync.py` (in `alix_studio_lite/`): it says which side
changed each file and whether each plan is still its config's (a config edited
and its re-planning failed leaves the old plan here); `pull` brings ALIX's
changes into Lite, `push` brings Lite's here. Lite's test suite fails while the
two differ. A sequence plan is re-made with its task: plan the task with its
`inspect_before_*` flag true, then false, and save the second as
`<task>_seq_toppra.*` (`Resource/reports/2026-10-28_lid_seat_close_trims/helpers/plan_close_mock43.sh`).

---

## Layout

```
plans/<fixture>/<source>/<task>_<arm>_<mode>.json
```

The two levels are not decoration — a plan is only meaningful for the fixture
it was planned against, and only trustworthy if you know what produced it.

### `<fixture>`

`commode_b`, `commode_c`, … — matches the fixture folder under
`config/<family>_cleaning/`. A plan planned against one fixture's geometry does
not transfer to another, even in the same family.

### `<source>` — what produced this plan

| source | meaning |
|---|---|
| `hardware` | planned and **executed on the arms**. The strongest evidence there is; the 13/13 runs live here. |
| `simulation` | planned against the sim. Kinematically valid, says nothing about servo tracking. |
| `moveit2` | generated by MoveIt 2 (planning pipeline + time parameterisation). |
| `controller` | generated by the RealMan controller's own planner, via the SDK. |
| `emulator` | generated against `alix_emulator`. Useful for pipeline tests; the emulator has no IK and models `movel_chain` as a timed no-op, so it proves dispatch, not motion. |
| `online_plans` | planned live during a session rather than ahead of time. |
| `mode_ab` | A/B comparisons between path modes — kept for the measurements, not for execution. |
| `post_fix` | re-planned after a specific fix, kept to show the difference. |

`moveit2`, `controller` and `emulator` are the sources going forward; the rest
came over from `butterfli_ws` and are kept with their provenance intact rather
than flattened, because "which planner produced this" is exactly the question
you need answered when a plan behaves differently on the arm.

---

## Where the other plan directory is, and why there are two

`core/python/src/alix_core/plans/` holds **four** plan JSONs that
`segment_verifier` treats as THE contract (PORT_PLAN.md §A.3) — a versioned
artifact of the ROS-free core, deliberately separate from this per-fixture
tree. `plan_roots()` searches this directory first, then that one;
`ALIX_PLANS_DIR` overrides both.

## History — one owner, twice over

**Port (2026-08).** `butterfli_ws` carried these twice: `cleaning_tasks/plans/`
(57 files) and `Resource/plans/` (38). Checked by content hash, **37 of the 38
were byte-identical** and the one that was not was `commode_c/hardware.zip`,
an archive of the directory beside it. Only one owner was ported, for the same
reason `alix_description` dropped its duplicate fixture meshes: two owners of
one artifact is how one gets regenerated and the other silently does not.

**Consolidation (2026-08-24, Newton).** The port had nevertheless kept the
task node's upstream dual-save — every plan into
`ros/orchestration/alix_tasks/plans/` and, for hardware plans, a second copy
here — so the same duplication grew back: 16 hardware plans existed in both
places, byte-identical. Ruling: save in the root `Resource/` folder only. The
node now writes here alone; the package tree's `plans/` moved here with its
history (`git mv`), the 16 duplicates were dropped from the package side, and
the gitignored `commode_c/ik_benchmark/` (26 MB of F80 solver output) moved
alongside so the tree stayed whole. `alix_tasks/plans/` no longer exists.

## Default plan mode: toppra (Newton 2026-10-05)

When nothing names a mode, every consumer runs the `_toppra` plans: the two senders (`dual_arm_trajectory_sender.py`, `arm_trajectory_sender.py`: `DEFAULT_MODE`, falling back to the folder's dominant mode only when it holds no toppra plan, and saying so), the orchestrator's lookups (`scheduler.find_plan`, `schedule_loader._find_plan` / `_find_compound_plan`: a recorded `_toppra` plan wins over the alphabetical or newest candidate) and the Studio (`PLAN_MODES` lists toppra first; Schedule & Run and DAC open on toppra whenever the catalog holds one; `/api/schedule-pairs` defaults to it). `--mode totg_ruckig` still selects the older plans explicitly. On `commode_c/hardware` the toppra set covers every schedule row except rows 0 and 2 (regions 34 and 21, recorded in the older modes only); `lid_open_toppra.json` and `seat_open_toppra.json` were generated into `commode_c/hardware` on 2026-10-05 17:56 from the live configs (the P20 choreography: left lifts, right depth-gap check, right finishes; DRAFT mirrored poses, teach + certify before hardware); the seat plan is seeded at the lid row's end state (rest, plates 0.15, hands as the lid row leaves them), the lid plan at rest with the plates at 0.15.
